unit.title: Introduction to Electrical Energy and DC Circuits

title: KVL/KCL practice and network-reduction techniques
summary: Three-mesh KVL and source-power calculation; two-node KCL analysis; series/parallel reduction rules for R, L and C; two equivalent-resistance practice networks; and a separately labelled PankusDesk worked continuation of the incomplete A–B problem.
transcription_policy: Notebook order and meaning are preserved; grammar and awkward English are lightly cleaned. Worked equations and numerical results are kept source-faithful. Where a handwritten intermediate sign conflicts with the equation immediately before and after it, the discrepancy is called out explicitly rather than silently changed. Incomplete network-reduction working is left incomplete rather than guessed.

blocks.label: PankusDesk worked continuation
blocks.title: Complete the A–B equivalent-resistance reduction
paragraphs: Work from the far right toward terminals A and B. At every stage, decide series or parallel from the node connections—not from how the resistors look on the page.
Series: the shared junction has no other branch, so the same current must pass through both resistors. Parallel: both branches connect between the same two nodes.

blocks.text: Step 1 — Start from the original network
Keep the original topology unchanged and begin at the extreme right, where the first series pair is unambiguous.

blocks.alt: NRS worked-continuation diagram of the original A–B resistor network: 2 ohm input resistors at A and B, 4 ohm and 5 ohm vertical branches, a 1.5 ohm upper resistor, a diagonal 4 ohm branch, a 3 ohm lower-right resistor, and two 2 ohm resistors at the far right.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 1 — Given A–B network

blocks.text: Step 2 — Combine the two rightmost \(2\,\Omega\) resistors

The upper-right \(2\,\Omega\) resistor and the right vertical \(2\,\Omega\) resistor share a junction with no other branch. They therefore carry the same current and are in series, giving \(2+2=4\,\Omega\).

blocks.alt: NRS reduction step showing the two far-right 2 ohm resistors replaced by one outer 4 ohm branch, while the diagonal 4 ohm branch, 3 ohm lower branch, 5 ohm vertical branch, 1.5 ohm resistor, and left-side network remain unchanged.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 2 — Rightmost series pair becomes 4 Ω

blocks.text: The new outer \(4\,\Omega\) branch and the diagonal \(4\,\Omega\) branch connect between the same upper-middle and lower-right nodes. They are parallel, so \(4\parallel4=2\,\Omega\).

blocks.alt: NRS reduction step showing the two parallel 4 ohm right-side branches replaced by one 2 ohm diagonal branch from the upper-middle node to the lower-right node, with the bottom 3 ohm resistor still present.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 3 — Parallel 4 Ω branches become 2 Ω

blocks.text: Step 4 — Form a \(5\,\Omega\) path on the right
After Step 3, the new \(2\,\Omega\) branch and the bottom \(3\,\Omega\) resistor meet at the lower-right node, where no other branch remains. They are therefore in series: \(2+3=5\,\Omega\).

blocks.alt: NRS reduction step showing two separate 5 ohm branches between the second upper node and the common lower node: the original vertical 5 ohm resistor and a new outer 5 ohm branch obtained from the 2 ohm plus 3 ohm series path.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 4 — The 2 Ω and 3 Ω path becomes 5 Ω

blocks.text: Both \(5\,\Omega\) branches now connect between exactly the same two nodes, so they are in parallel: \(5\parallel5=2.5\,\Omega\).

blocks.alt: NRS reduction step showing the two 5 ohm branches replaced by a single 2.5 ohm vertical branch, leaving the 1.5 ohm upper resistor, the left vertical 4 ohm resistor, and the 2 ohm input resistors at A and B.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 5 — Parallel 5 Ω branches become 2.5 Ω

blocks.text: The \(1.5\,\Omega\) resistor and the new \(2.5\,\Omega\) branch are now in series, because their shared upper-right junction has no other branch. Their equivalent is \(1.5+2.5=4\,\Omega\), which lies in parallel with the original vertical \(4\,\Omega\) resistor.

blocks.alt: NRS reduction step showing two 4 ohm branches in parallel between the same upper and lower nodes, with a 2 ohm resistor from A to the upper node and a 2 ohm resistor from B to the lower node.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 6 — The middle path becomes 4 Ω

blocks.text: The two middle \(4\,\Omega\) branches are parallel, so they reduce to \(2\,\Omega\). The remaining network is then three \(2\,\Omega\) resistors in series from A to B: \(R_{AB}=2+2+2=6\,\Omega\).

blocks.alt: NRS final reduction showing 4 ohms in parallel with 4 ohms becoming a 2 ohm middle resistor, then three 2 ohm resistors in series between A and B, and finally one 6 ohm equivalent resistor between A and B.
blocks.caption: PankusDesk worked continuation · Step 7 — Final equivalent resistance R_AB = 6 Ω
